results.summary: Stage 1 done for DirectSun. Root approved by his card of 2:27 AM PST 2026-11-28 (OWNER:1795861938602549019), with his two changes folded in as on Graffiti: 'plans around on every sunlit map' softened to 'feels wherever it shines, and on many maps plans around' (the mechanic still runs on every sunlit map), and a new sentence that shade is not always wanted: the sun's warmth is felt too (the code adds the sun to felt temperature at every temperature), so where a mountain's shadow will fall is a major concern when the player picks where to build. a_mountain_drawn answered (a): a mountain's long shadow is drawn on the ground as a soft dark band (d_mountain_drawn_band, OWNER:1795861940796843369); the greatbole trial's own ruling for trees stays open. How far a mountain's shadow may reach at a low sun is the edge for stage 2.

quick_look.why: The question is what a shadow should take from crops and panels, and the mountain band is not built; no save shows a crop or a panel reacting to shade, so a look would show only that today nothing reacts, which the ask already states.

results.summary: Stage 2 Argue the edge for DirectSun. Taken without asking (Evidence-for-Ask, OWNER-shard event 1795862831529445191): a mountain's band reaches as far as the one geometry casts it, longer where the sun stands lower, with no extra length rule, because his card of 2:27 AM PST answered the flood doubt by softening the root and making unwanted mountain shade a planning concern (d_mountain_reach_geometry). One ask sent, a_shade_takes: what a cast shadow takes from the ground it falls on, (a) only the warmth that pawns feel or (b) also the light that crops and solar panels use, in every lee and under every crown by the one geometry. As built, no shade touches crops or panels, so under (a) the root's 'field' is false and unwanted shade costs mostly a colder outdoor workplace. A fresh Opus reviewer struck the first draft (it said shade touches only pawn heat, but shade also dims sun-powered work tables) and passed it after four fixes.
